name: SIMKER — Sistem Informasi Kerja Sama
description: Cooperation management system built from the ground up to record and track the university's institutional partnerships — MoU, MoA, and implementation agreements — across program-study, faculty, and university level.
challenge: Cooperation documents (MoU, MoA, and implementation records) were tracked manually across program studies, faculties, and the university, making it hard to see status, ownership, or expiry at a glance.
solution: Designed and built a role-based information system from scratch — requirements analysis, workflow design, database schema, and a CodeIgniter 3 application that lets each level (program study, faculty, university) manage its own cooperation records within one shared structure.
result: Cooperation records for all three institutional levels are now centralized, searchable, and auditable in a single system that is still in active production use.

name: SIMLITABMAS — Sistem Informasi Penelitian & Pengabdian Masyarakat
description: Research and community-service information system built from scratch to manage the full grant lifecycle for lecturers and students — from proposal submission through review to LPPM funding.
challenge: Research and community-service proposals had no structured digital workflow, making it difficult for LPPM (the research & community-service institute) to review submissions and track funding decisions consistently.
solution: Built the workflow end-to-end: lecturer/student submits a proposal → reviewer is assigned → review is recorded → proposal is selected → funding is disbursed by LPPM. Covered requirements analysis, workflow design, development, database, testing, and deployment.
result: Proposal submission, review, and funding decisions now run through one traceable system instead of manual, paper-based coordination.

name: University Website Ecosystem
description: Development, maintenance, performance optimization, technical SEO, security, and content-structure management across 20+ WordPress websites spanning the university, its faculties, and study programs.
challenge: 20+ independently run WordPress sites across faculties and study programs meant inconsistent SEO health, uneven performance, and recurring security exposure — with no single owner keeping them aligned.
solution: Manage the ecosystem end-to-end: WordPress development and theme/content structure, Screaming Frog crawl audits, on-page SEO fixes, Core Web Vitals optimization, and security hardening — applied consistently across every site in the network.
result: A 20+ site network kept online, secure, and technically healthy, with SEO and performance treated as an ongoing process rather than a one-time fix.

name: University GA4 Analytics Dashboard
description: AI-assisted analytics dashboard that aggregates 23 Google Analytics 4 properties across the university and four faculties into one reporting view covering demographics, traffic acquisition, content engagement, and conversion.
challenge: With 23 separate GA4 properties across the university and its faculties, pulling a combined traffic and engagement picture meant checking each property individually — too slow for regular stakeholder reporting.
solution: Built a Google Apps Script–based dashboard that pulls and aggregates data from all 23 GA4 properties into a single view, structured around demographics, traffic acquisition, engagement, and conversion.
result: Traffic and engagement across the entire university web ecosystem can now be reviewed from one dashboard instead of 23 separate GA4 properties.

name: ADELE — Automatic Distribution and Equalization Engine
description: Pension-fund distribution application at PT Fresnel Perdana Mandiri, where I developed and integrated a pension-fund calculation module and improved the front-end for usability.
challenge: The team needed a reliable pension-fund calculation module integrated into an existing distribution engine, alongside front-end usability issues that made the tool harder to operate.
solution: Developed and integrated the pension-fund calculation module, then reworked parts of the front-end to improve functionality and ease of use.
result: A working calculation module integrated into ADELE's production workflow, with an improved front-end experience for its users.

name: University Electronic Journal (OJS)
description: Installation, administration, and security maintenance of the university's Open Journal Systems (OJS) platform, including detecting and cleaning up spam and illegal-content injections.
challenge: The journal platform was targeted by content injection — including gambling-spam content hidden inside the database — which threatened both search visibility and platform integrity.
solution: Ran technical database-query investigations to locate the injected content, removed it, and restored the integrity of the journal system, alongside ongoing platform administration.
result: Journal platform integrity restored and kept clean through ongoing monitoring, as part of ongoing administration of the university's digital platforms.

name: Digital Correspondence & Library Information System
description: Day-to-day operation of the university's digital correspondence (persuratan) system and its SLiMS 9/Bulian library information system.
challenge: Official correspondence and library records needed a reliable digital system that stays available and accurate for daily administrative use.
solution: Operate and maintain both platforms directly — availability, data integrity, and day-to-day administrative support for staff using them.
result: Correspondence and library records run on stable, actively maintained systems rather than manual processes.

name: Digital Infrastructure Administration
description: Installation and administration of the university's supporting digital infrastructure: Nextcloud (cloud storage), EPrints 3 (repository), and the internal help-desk/HESK support system.
challenge: Cloud storage, the institutional repository, and internal IT support each needed a dedicated, properly configured platform that staff could rely on.
solution: Installed, configured, and administer all three platforms, keeping them available and handling routine maintenance and support requests.
result: Staff have working cloud storage, a functioning repository, and a help-desk channel for technical support, all kept running by ongoing administration.
